messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — PR #10234 (routing cache eviction) is green but I'm holding merge until we have an RFC link and an architecture sign-off. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/10234
maya: I pasted a minimal summary into the PR description but want a lightweight arch blessing before merge. @sam @liam can you eyeball? :eyes:
deploy-bot: CI passed — unit/integration/e2e all green (build 8921) :white_check_mark:
nora: which RFC should we link here? I remember a draft about 'kv-cache routing' — is that the one?
maya: yes — draft lives at https://docs.internal/redwood/rfcs/kv-cache-routing-draft.md (still WIP). Core decision is there but it hasn't been formally reviewed yet.
sam: quick ask — please add a 3–4 line architecture summary in the PR description that calls out failure modes, fallback behavior, and canary plan. Also include the RFC link and owner.
dave: if the summary is present and SLO impact is small, can arch do a lightweight bless instead of full RFC signoff? We've got a release window tomorrow.
maya: SLO delta estimated around +0.3% p99 tail. It touches cross-tenant cache routing so I get the caution. I'll update the PR now.
maya: suggested snippet to paste into PR description:
```
Architecture summary: routes warm KV-cache hits to local shards; on miss we fall back to remote shard asynchronously to avoid blocking the critical path. Repeated miss patterns trigger throttling and route to CPU fallback.
Impact: estimated p99 +0.3%.
Canary: 2h at 10% traffic, monitor latency & error-rate dashboards.
RFC: https://docs.internal/redwood/rfcs/kv-cache-routing-draft.md (owner: Maya)
```
sam: thanks — please add explicit fallback steps and the canary monitoring links (latency, errors, infra alerts). If you add that I'll give a lightweight LGTM.
maya: updated PR description with full snippet and monitoring links:
```
Architecture summary: This change routes warm KV-cache hits to local shards and falls back to remote shards on miss. Fallback is async so it doesn't add tail latency to the hot path; repeated misses are throttled and routed to a CPU fallback path.
Impact: estimated p99 +0.3%.
Canary: 2h at 10% traffic. Monitor: https://dashboards.internal/kv-cache-latency, https://dashboards.internal/kv-cache-errors.
Rollback: immediate traffic revert + force-deploy previous commit. Runbook: https://runbooks.internal/canary-playbook
RFC: https://docs.internal/redwood/rfcs/kv-cache-routing-draft.md (owner: Maya)
```
sam: OK — lightweight arch LGTM. Please ensure the RFC link is visible at the top of the PR description and tag @sam for the final quick check. After that we can merge during the scheduled window.
nora: do we need an explicit rollback runbook entry in the PR or is the runbook link sufficient?
sam: runbook link is fine but add a one-line rollback summary in the PR for quick scanning.
maya: added one-line rollback summary and pinged ops for canary watch. Ready for final check.
arch-bot: RFC status: DRAFT — awaiting formal review. Tagged for visibility.
sam: final check complete, arch gives LGTM. @maya go ahead to merge once the release window opens; keep the canary and monitoring as documented.
deploy-bot: merge scheduled for 2026-04-02T10:00:00Z per release calendar :gear:
liam: thanks everyone — appreciate the speedy turn on this. :tada:
